Let me analyze the model predictions:

- median_prediction: mean 0.425, first_third_mean 0.192, last_third_mean 0.4707, last_window 0.3861
  - Prediction is 0 at tipping point, 1 far away
  - The first third has low predictions (0.192), meaning close to tipping
  - The last third has higher predictions (0.4707), meaning further from tipping
  - The last window is 0.3861

- p_critical: mean 0.3771, max 0.7012, last_window 0.3616, last_third_mean 0.3317, share_of_windows_above_half 0.3077
  - p_critical is probability that system is near tipping
  - Last window p_critical is 0.3616 (below 0.5)
  - Last third mean is 0.3317 (below 0.5)
  - Only 30.77% of windows are above 0.5

So the model predictions show:
- Early windows (first third) had low median predictions (close to tipping, ~0.19)
- Later windows have higher median predictions (further from tipping, ~0.47)
- The last window prediction is 0.3861, which is below 0.5 but not extremely close to 0
- p_critical for last window is 0.3616, below 0.5 threshold
- Only ~31% of windows have p_critical above 0.5

The trend in predictions is going UP (from 0.192 to 0.4707), meaning the system is moving AWAY from the tipping point over time. The last window is at 0.3861 with p_critical 0.3616.

This suggests "no_alert" - the end of the series does not look close to tipping. The predictions are increasing (moving away from 0), and p_critical is below 0.5 for the last window.

Wait, let me reconsider. The median prediction for the last window is 0.3861. The scale is 0 at tipping, 1 far away. So 0.3861 is somewhat close to 0 but not extremely close. And p_critical is 0.3616, which is below 0.5.

The key question is about "the end of the series" - the last window. The last window has:
- median prediction: 0.3861 (moderately close to tipping but not very close)
- p_critical: 0.3616 (below 0.5, so more likely not critical)

Also important: the trend is going in the direction of AWAY from tipping (predictions increasing from first third to last third).

I'll go with "no_alert" with moderate confidence.
